_rule: Ranked by impact (commissioning, atlas, public result, physics, research), then cost (laptop before box). Every accession must be in the Master Inventory. Edit this file to add or retire a job; the inventory renders it. Each job carries plain, needs, estimate and record (written for followers); help_wanted lists the gaps public data cannot close. CANON/roadmap.py writes ROADMAP.md from this file.

jobs.job: IAM-A commissioning: find the cause of the across-labs failure (three deep EMSeq LAB02 runs read low), development read of other file parts
jobs.ready: scored; held under the stopping rule
jobs.plain: Find out why three files from one laboratory read low in the IAM-A instrument test, so the test can be finished honestly.
jobs.needs: a rented computer for about 3 hours
jobs.stands: the test is written and its rules are fixed; waiting for a rented computer to be available at a fair price

jobs.job: Neutrophil reference from a second laboratory: build GSE124565, test GSE88824, GSE118144, GSE122244
jobs.plain: Build the healthy white-blood-cell reference from a second laboratory, so Met-A no longer leans on one lab's donors.
jobs.stands: the data are found; their files are being checked

jobs.job: IAM-A on other-lab healthy neutrophils (RRBS) and same DNA on arrays and WGBS
jobs.plain: Read healthy white blood cells from other laboratories with IAM-A, and the same DNA on two kinds of measurement.
jobs.estimate: priced in the ledger before it starts
jobs.stands: the data are found; their files are to be checked

jobs.job: Whole-blood bar 7 on cord blood with flow counts (assess newborn caveat first)
jobs.plain: Test Met-A's blood-cell counting against counts made by a cell counter, using newborn cord blood, after checking that newborn blood is a fair stand-in.
jobs.stands: the data are found; first we check whether newborn blood is a fair stand-in

jobs.job: Atlas v2.1: rebuild with second-lab and new cell types; split GSE224807 donors half build, half test
jobs.plain: Rebuild the atlas as version 2.1, with second and third laboratories and new cell types, then check it on data it never saw.
jobs.needs: a rented computer for about a day
jobs.estimate: about $40-100, priced in the ledger before it starts
jobs.stands: the plan is locked: which samples build the map and which are kept back to test it

jobs.job: Colon epithelium from an independent laboratory into the atlas
jobs.plain: Add colon lining cells from a laboratory independent of the atlas sources.
jobs.stands: the data are found; we are confirming the donors were healthy and are not already in the atlas

jobs.job: Lung stroma culture check before atlas entry
jobs.plain: Measure how much growing cells in a dish changes them, before dish-grown lung cells go anywhere near the atlas.
jobs.stands: first lab done (about 1 in 9 sites drift in a dish); two more labs' data are downloading

jobs.job: Lung tissue test: four lung sets tested (1 scored, 3 not suitable); next lung test waits for atlas v2.1 and the culture check
jobs.plain: Try lung cancer again once the atlas describes the lung's support cells well enough.
jobs.stands: on hold until the atlas has better lung support cells

jobs.job: Liver fingerprint replication on fresh data
jobs.plain: Repeat the liver cancer result on fresh data from different patients.
jobs.needs: a rented computer (about 5 terabytes of sequencing)
jobs.estimate: about $30-50, priced in the ledger before it starts
jobs.stands: the data are found; not yet downloaded

jobs.job: Colon adenomas: does Met-A rise before cancer?
jobs.plain: Colon polyps, the step before cancer: does the reading already rise there?
jobs.stands: the data are on our storage; the test is not yet designed

jobs.job: Neurons: sorted-only reference sealed on two unread laboratories
jobs.plain: Brain cells that stopped dividing decades ago: a test of the physics on two laboratories' data nobody has read with our instruments.
jobs.estimate: priced in the ledger before it starts
jobs.stands: the data are found; the healthy reference is built

jobs.job: Neurons on Met-A (both instruments on neurons)
jobs.plain: Read brain cells with Met-A too, so both instruments look at the same cell type.
jobs.stands: the data are found; their files are to be checked

jobs.job: Sex balance: female donors across blood cell types
jobs.plain: Add more female donors across blood cell types, so the healthy reference is not mostly men.
jobs.stands: one candidate data set; checking that its laboratory is independent

jobs.job: EPIC v2 read check for Stage 1 (opens thymocytes for the atlas and EPIC v2 sets in S3)
jobs.plain: Teach the first stage of the chain to read the newest chip, which opens thymus cells, where one kind of leukemia starts, for the atlas.

help_wanted.ask: Healthy neutrophils sequenced whole-genome (bisulfite or enzymatic) in a laboratory other than the Loyfer group, three or more donors.
help_wanted.why: An open test of the IAM-A instrument: does a healthy person from another laboratory read as healthy?

help_wanted.ask: Methylation of fresh, never dish-grown lung fibroblasts or lung smooth muscle (sorted cells; arrays or sequencing).
help_wanted.why: Every public sample of these cells was grown in a dish first; fresh ones would let lung cancer be tested fairly.

help_wanted.ask: Whole-blood EPIC arrays with cell counts from flow cytometry, from a laboratory independent of the reference groups.
help_wanted.why: Met-A is commissioned on isolated neutrophils; whole blood, the real blood test, needs counted cells to check against.

help_wanted.ask: Methylation after weeks of methionine restriction (cells or animals).
help_wanted.why: A second, independent way to test the physics: cutting the methyl supply should move the IAM-A reading by an amount the physics predicts in advance.
